_note: The RIVALS' moments (session P1, GDD 4.9.5; format in README.md). A rival met in data/cast.json rivals.met_min races becomes a person in the Rivals thread (at most rivals.max). Topic `rival`: on the evening after a race you both ran, with the chance rivals.note_chance one of them writes (StoryletSystem._post_rival_note; never a stop, outside the 2-4 a week). Sender conditions: rival_race beat (you finished ahead of them) / lost, rival_streak = their wins over you in a row, rival_wins = your wins over them in a row; their memory remembers 'met_up' and 'nemesis' (the rival who always beats you: started after three losses in a row, ended by beating them). Session L3a (the sort, docs/L3_SORT.md, user 2026-10-25): every rival message is FEED (it asks nothing); the chain lives in the rival's memory, set by the message itself (`effects`, story state). No line describes how the race went beyond what the game knows (who finished ahead). Youth rivals are fictional (minors).

text: Hey, it's {from}. We keep ending up in the same races, so I thought I'd say hi. Good race today.
{from} here, from today's race. We've raced each other a few times now. Respect.
You got me today. Next time.
OK, today was yours. Enjoy it, it won't last.
Good race. I died in the home straight. You didn't.
Good race today. Seriously, good run.
That one was mine. You're getting faster though, I can feel it.
That's three in a row now. Not that I'm counting. OK, I'm counting.
Again! You should try going earlier. Or later. Or not at all, ha.
Same story. I'm starting to feel bad for you. A little.
Still mine.
You know what I'm going to say.
...OK. You finally did it. Congratulations. Really.
Well. That happened. Enjoy it. I'm going to train twice as hard now.
Three times in a row you've beaten me. I'd love to know what you do in training.
OK, you're the one to beat now. I'll be on your shoulder next time.
{pb}! You're getting dangerous.
Saw your time. Great run. Now I have to go faster too.
Heard you're injured. Sorry. It's boring out there without you. Get well.
Someone said you're out for a while. It isn't the same. Come back soon.
